A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CausalPFN work. Their main text, mathematical appendices, experimental tables, and figures are readable and support comparison, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original CATE/ATE benchmark evaluations, marketing uplift experiments, TabPFN fine-tuning comparisons, and synthetic and benchmark calibration analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds dataset-size sensitivity experiments and a head-to-head comparison with Do-PFN.

M1.justification: The causal prior, 20-layer transformer, histogram objective, two-stage training, retrieval procedure, and temperature calibration are retained. Matching Section 4 and Appendix D.2 across versions establishes that the expanded experiments do not introduce a new CausalPFN procedure.

E1.justification: The training sources, named benchmarks, marketing tasks, and polynomial/sinusoidal families remain. New Appendix D.3 extends polynomial evaluation to high-dimensional inputs, including 500 and 1,000 covariates beyond the stated 100-covariate training range. Increased realization and sample counts are separate protocol changes.

E2.justification: New Appendix E evaluates the directly competing Do-PFN on all four ground-truth benchmarks. DA-Learner also enters the tuned and untuned CATE/ATE comparisons in Tables 1 and 6; in v1 its reported participation was confined to marketing comparisons.

E3.justification: Each Lalonde cohort expands from 10 to 100 realizations, increasing the pooled evaluation from 130 to 310. ATE aggregation changes from mean relative error to average rank. EconML tuning changes from a small grid search to a 900-second FLAML search, with cubic rather than quadratic expansion for DR/DML and additional final-model tuning. New sensitivity experiments introduce controlled row/feature sweeps. The stated Qini normalizer also changes from lambda to lambda(1), without changed marketing scores.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 systematically tests how PEHE responds to sample size and covariate dimensionality, using 10–10,000 rows and 1–1,000 covariates while controlling the other dimension. These scalability analyses were absent from v1. Existing distribution-shift calibration and TabPFN fine-tuning analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions already report standard errors and calibration error bars. v2 specifies 50 differently seeded polynomial datasets per sensitivity configuration and clarifies in its checklist that benchmark and calibration error bars represent one-standard-error uncertainty across dataset realizations. This adds statistical documentation without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation method.

E6.justification: The tuned and untuned benchmark tables substantially revise scores and rankings. For example, CausalPFN's Lalonde CPS/PSID PEHE changes from 8.83/13.98 to 8.96/14.40, in thousands, under the expanded realization counts; these are not same-setting performance changes. Tables 4–5 add sensitivity results, and Table 8 adds Do-PFN results. Marketing scores and the existing calibration curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The consistency and KL-equivalence results remain, but Appendices A–C refine prior-level identifiability and the measurable quotient construction, correct an overly strong biconditional in the proof, and explicitly scope density assumptions to the KL argument. v1's Equation 43 claiming exact posterior equality at a global optimum is replaced by an approximate near-optimum statement.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the performance contribution from superior average benchmark performance to best average CATE rank and competitive ATE performance. The core amortization, uncertainty, and deployment contributions remain. The abstract retains its broader superiority wording, so the qualification is not applied consistently throughout v2.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 newly attributes the shrinking advantage at high dimensionality to training exposure limited to 100 covariates and suggests broader training. Appendix E interprets differences from Do-PFN through prediction targets and prior identifiability. Existing limitations concerning ignorability, finite-sample guarantees, and large-table retrieval remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds inference hardware specifications, revised FLAML settings, PyPI package access information, and a repository CSV link replacing the previous OpenML-catalogue link. The model training recipe remains unchanged. The new checklist introduces a hardware inconsistency: it states one A100 for base training, while Appendix D.2 still states four.

R1.justification: Section 6 and new Appendix E substantially expand positioning against concurrent Do-PFN, contrasting its interventional-outcome target and reported lack of enforced prior identifiability with CausalPFN. Additional citations support histogram losses, measurable-space arguments, FLAML, and latency-sensitive applications. Bibliographic publication updates otherwise refer to retained works.

P1.justification: Appendices A–C are extensively rewritten and reorganized, including moving the quotient-space definition and restructuring the proof exposition. Main-text notation and prose are edited, while dedicated sensitivity, inference-speed, and concurrent-work sections, acknowledgements, and a checklist are added. The main seven-section narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4, 5, and 8, redraws Figure 1 with revised axes and legend, and changes benchmark-table columns and highlighting. Calibration figures are retained with revised captions and placement. These are localized display changes within the existing overall visual format.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, broader baseline tuning, more Lalonde realizations, sensitivity tests, and the Do-PFN comparison strengthen the empirical support. Mathematical corrections and the narrower introductory ATE claim improve precision. The gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: the abstract retains broader performance wording, and the new compute checklist contradicts Appendix D.2. Overall, the evidence supports a modest quality improvement.
